stem: 'Natural vegetation' refers to:
options: Plant life that grows naturally without human help (virgin vegetation)
solution: Natural (virgin) vegetation grows on its own without human interference, undisturbed for a long time.

stem: The term 'flora' refers to the __________ of a region.
solution: 'Flora' refers to the plants of a particular region, while 'fauna' refers to its animals.

stem: The animals of a particular region are collectively called its:
solution: 'Fauna' refers to the animal life of a region.

stem: India is regarded as one of the world's __________ countries in terms of biodiversity.
solution: India is one of the world's twelve mega-biodiverse countries, rich in plant and animal species.

stem: The type of vegetation that grows in areas with more than 200 cm of rainfall is:
solution: Tropical evergreen forests grow in high-rainfall (over 200 cm) regions like the Western Ghats and the North-East.

stem: Tropical evergreen forests are called 'evergreen' because:
options: Trees do not shed all their leaves at the same time, so the forest looks green all year
They are always covered in snow
solution: In tropical evergreen forests, trees shed leaves at different times, so the forest never looks bare and appears green throughout the year.

stem: Valuable trees like rosewood, ebony and mahogany are found in which forests?
solution: Rosewood, ebony and mahogany are hardwoods found in the tropical evergreen (rain)forests.

stem: The most widespread forests in India, occurring in areas with 70-200 cm rainfall, are the:
solution: Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests are the most widespread forests in India, found in areas of moderate rainfall.

stem: Deciduous trees are so called because they:
options: Shed their leaves in the dry season
solution: Deciduous trees shed their leaves for about six to eight weeks in the dry season to conserve water.

stem: The most important timber tree of the moist tropical deciduous forest is:
solution: Teak is the most important tree of the moist tropical deciduous forests; sal is another key species.

stem: In regions with less than 70 cm rainfall, the natural vegetation is:
solution: Thorn forests and scrubs, with plants adapted to dryness, grow in semi-arid regions receiving less than 70 cm of rainfall.

stem: Plants of the thorn forests, like acacia and cacti, have adaptations such as:
options: Long roots, thick stems and thorns/waxy leaves to conserve water
solution: Thorn-forest plants have long roots, thick fleshy stems and small thorny or waxy leaves to reduce water loss.

stem: Montane (mountain) forests change with altitude. The forests of high altitudes above the tree line become:
options: Alpine vegetation and then tundra (mosses, lichens)
solution: With increasing altitude, montane forests give way to alpine vegetation and finally to tundra (mosses and lichens) near the snow line.

stem: Coniferous trees such as pine, deodar and silver fir are found in:
options: The montane (mountain) forests at higher altitudes
solution: Coniferous trees like pine, deodar and silver fir grow in the temperate montane forests of the Himalayas.

stem: Mangrove (tidal) forests grow in areas influenced by:
options: Tides, in deltas and coastal wetlands
solution: Mangrove/tidal forests grow in the tidal, salt-water areas of deltas and coastal wetlands.

stem: The 'Sundari' tree, which gives the Sundarbans their name, grows in which type of forest?
solution: The Sundari tree, characteristic of the mangrove forests of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, gives the Sundarbans their name.

stem: The distribution of natural vegetation depends mainly on:
options: Relief (land, soil) and climate (temperature, sunlight, precipitation)
solution: Natural vegetation is determined by relief (land and soil) and climate (temperature, photoperiod/sunlight and precipitation).

stem: The government programme launched in 1973 to protect tigers is called:
solution: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to protect the endangered Bengal tiger and its habitat.

stem: The Asiatic lion in India is found in its natural habitat only in the:
solution: The Asiatic lion survives in the wild only in the Gir forest of Gujarat.

stem: The one-horned rhinoceros is famously protected in which national park?
solution: The one-horned rhinoceros is chiefly protected in Kaziranga National Park in Assam.

stem: Areas set aside to protect and conserve wildlife are called:
options: National parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves
solution: Wildlife is conserved in national parks, wildlife sanctuaries and biosphere reserves.

stem: Species that are in danger of extinction are called:
solution: Endangered species are those whose numbers have fallen so low that they are at risk of extinction.

stem: Species found only in a particular area and nowhere else are called:
solution: Endemic species are those restricted to a particular area and found nowhere else naturally.

stem: The migratory bird that famously visits India (e.g. wetlands) in winter is the:
solution: The Siberian crane is a well-known migratory bird that visits Indian wetlands during winter.

stem: A major threat to India's natural vegetation and wildlife is:
solution: Deforestation, poaching/hunting and the destruction of habitats are the main threats to natural vegetation and wildlife.

stem: The variety of plant and animal life in a region is called its:
solution: Biodiversity refers to the variety of plant and animal species found in a region.

stem: Forests are ecologically important because they:
options: Maintain balance, provide oxygen, protect soil and support wildlife
solution: Forests maintain ecological balance, provide oxygen, regulate climate, protect soil and shelter wildlife.

stem: Which of the following pairs (species — habitat) is correctly matched?
solution: The one-horned rhino lives in Kaziranga. The Asiatic lion is in Gir, tigers in various reserves (e.g. Sundarbans, Corbett), not Gir.

stem: The vegetation of the delta and coastal areas that can survive in salt water is:
solution: Mangrove forests, adapted to survive in tidal salt water, grow in deltas and coastal wetlands.

stem: The alpine vegetation and grasslands are used by pastoralists such as the __________ for grazing in summer.
solution: The high alpine meadows are used for summer grazing by mountain pastoralists such as the Gujjars and Gaddis.

stem: Which type of forest sheds its leaves to conserve water during the dry season?
solution: Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests shed their leaves in the dry season to conserve water.

stem: India's rich biodiversity is due to its:
options: Varied relief and climate, from tropical to alpine conditions
solution: India's diverse relief and climate — from tropical coasts to alpine mountains — support a great variety of plant and animal life.

stem: The 'photoperiod' that affects plant growth refers to the:
solution: The photoperiod is the duration of sunlight; it influences the growth of trees and other plants.

stem: Conservation of forests and wildlife is important because it:
options: Maintains ecological balance and preserves biodiversity for the future
solution: Conserving forests and wildlife maintains ecological balance and preserves biodiversity for present and future generations.

stem: Large protected areas that conserve the plant and animal life along with the traditional lifestyle of the inhabitants are called:
solution: Biosphere reserves are large protected areas that conserve biodiversity and the traditional lifestyle of local inhabitants.

stem: The main reason many species in India have become endangered is:
options: Human activities like hunting, deforestation and pollution
solution: Human activities — hunting/poaching, deforestation, habitat destruction and pollution — have made many species endangered.

stem: The vegetation type found in the highest Himalayan reaches, near the snowline, is:
solution: Near the snowline in the high Himalayas, the vegetation is tundra — mosses and lichens.

stem: Which of the following is a tropical evergreen forest region of India?
options: The Western Ghats and the North-East
solution: Tropical evergreen forests are found in the high-rainfall regions of the Western Ghats and the North-East.

stem: The natural vegetation of a region and its wildlife are closely linked because:
options: Wildlife depends on vegetation for food and shelter
solution: Wildlife depends on natural vegetation for food, shelter and habitat, so the two are ecologically interlinked.

stem: The IUCN 'Red List' is used to:
solution: The IUCN Red List identifies and classifies species according to their risk of extinction (threatened, endangered, etc.).

stem: Human interference has led to the reduction of natural vegetation cover mainly through:
options: Expansion of agriculture, settlement and industry
solution: The spread of agriculture, settlements and industry has cleared much of India's natural vegetation.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a bird sanctuary in India?
solution: The Bharatpur (Keoladeo) sanctuary in Rajasthan is famous as a bird sanctuary, especially for migratory birds.

stem: The felling of trees for timber, fuel and land has resulted in:
options: Loss of forest cover and threats to wildlife
solution: The large-scale felling of trees has reduced forest cover and threatened the wildlife that depends on it.

stem: The forests that remain green throughout the year and receive very heavy rainfall are found in:
options: The Western Ghats, North-East and Andaman & Nicobar Islands
solution: The tropical evergreen (rain)forests are found in the very wet regions of the Western Ghats, North-East and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

stem: Which of the following is a step taken by the government to conserve wildlife?
options: Setting up national parks and launching Project Tiger and Project Elephant
solution: The government conserves wildlife by setting up national parks and sanctuaries and launching programmes like Project Tiger and Project Elephant.

stem: Which type of forest yields the commercially valuable teak and sal?
solution: The tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests yield commercially valuable timber like teak and sal.

stem: The main reason India has such varied natural vegetation is its:
solution: India's varied climate and physiography give rise to its wide range of natural vegetation, from rainforests to deserts.

stem: The role of sanctuaries and national parks is to:
options: Protect wildlife and their habitats from human interference
solution: National parks and sanctuaries protect wildlife and their natural habitats from hunting and other human interference.

stem: The government programme launched in 1992 to protect elephants and their habitats is called:
solution: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 to protect elephants, their habitats and migration corridors.

stem: The overall theme of 'Natural Vegetation and Wildlife' is that:
options: India has diverse vegetation and rich wildlife that must be conserved
solution: The chapter explains India's diverse natural vegetation and rich wildlife, and stresses the need to conserve them.
